summary: Consent requirement for disclosure of PII from education records; 'reasonable methods' (physical/technological access controls) so school officials access only records with legitimate educational interest (99.31(a)(1)(ii)); disclosure recordkeeping (99.32).
applies_to: Educational agencies and institutions that receive funds under any ED-administered program (99.1). This includes nearly all public K-12 and Title IV colleges.
size_thresholds: No size threshold. It does not apply solely because students receive non-monetary benefits (99.1(b)), so many private K-12 schools that take no ED funds are outside FERPA.
status: In force. FERPA has no breach notification requirement.

summary: Written information security program with a Qualified Individual, risk assessment, access controls, encryption, MFA, pen testing/vuln scanning, IR plan, board reporting; plus FTC breach notice (314.4(j)).
applies_to: Postsecondary institutions and third-party servicers participating in Title IV. Each agreed in its Program Participation Agreement to comply with 16 CFR 314 (FSA Electronic Announcement GENERAL-23-09). 'Customer information' = information obtained in providing a financial service to a student (e.g., Title IV administration, institutional loans).
size_thresholds: 314.6: institutions holding customer information on fewer than 5,000 consumers are exempt from 314.4(b)(1) (written risk assessment), (d)(2) (continuous monitoring/pen testing), (h) (written IR plan) and (i) (annual board report). The 314.4(j) FTC notice applies only to events affecting 500 or more consumers.
status: In force. FSA enforces through annual compliance audits (findings affect Title IV administrative capability, 34 CFR 668.16(c)). FSA also encouraged adoption of NIST SP 800-171 (Dec 18, 2020 EA).

summary: Verifiable parental consent before collecting personal information from children under 13; new 312.8(b) requires a written information security program (designated coordinator, annual risk assessment, safeguards, testing). Ed-tech may rely on school authorization in limited cases.
applies_to: Operators of websites/online services directed to children under 13, or with actual knowledge (ed-tech vendors, K-12 platforms).
size_thresholds: The 'operator' definition excludes nonprofits exempt from FTC Act Section 5 (16 CFR 312.2). Security program is scaled to 'size, complexity, and nature and scope of activities.'
status: Amended rule 90 FR 16918 (Apr 22, 2025), effective June 23, 2025; compliance date Apr 22, 2026 (except 312.11(d)(1), (d)(4), (g)).

summary: Schools and libraries receiving E-Rate discounts must certify an internet safety policy and technology protection measures (filtering) and monitoring of minors' online activities (schools).
applies_to: K-12 schools, school districts and libraries receiving E-Rate discounts for internet access/internal connections.

summary: Administrative, physical and technical safeguards to ensure confidentiality, integrity and availability of ePHI; risk-based and scalable (164.306(b)).
applies_to: Universities with covered health care components (academic medical centers, clinics billing electronically) that designate as hybrid entities (45 CFR 164.105). Student health records covered by FERPA are excluded from PHI.
size_thresholds: No size exemption; 164.306(b)(2) lets entities factor size, complexity, capabilities and cost when choosing measures.
status: In force; eCFR text current as of 2026-09-23 unchanged by the Jan 2025 NPRM (see separate entry).

summary: Would require covered entities to report covered cyber incidents to CISA within 72 hours and ransom payments within 24 hours (proposed 226.5).
applies_to: Proposed 226.2(b)(9): LEAs, educational service agencies and SEAs with 1,000 or more students, and every IHE receiving Title IV funding.
size_thresholds: LEA/ESA/SEA: student population of 1,000 or more. IHE: any Title IV participant (no size floor). Otherwise, exceeding the SBA size standard.
status: PROPOSED ONLY. NPRM 89 FR 23644 (Apr 4, 2024). CISA held town halls (Feb 13 and May 26, 2026 notices) to refine scope. Fall 2025 Unified Agenda targeted a final rule for 09/2026. As of 2026-09-25 no final rule is in the Federal Register; CISA says it 'continues to work on the final rule.' Reporting is not yet mandatory.
